fatal_errors: The proposed polycrystalline compression-versus-tension comparison does not reconstruct the target single-crystal tensile study across crystallographic orientations, temperatures, and strain rates.
The supporting evidence concerns Al0.1CrCoFeNi, whose Al- and Co-dependent ordering behavior cannot substantiate short-range-order transitions in equiatomic FeNiCrMn.
The predicted compression-induced hardening and 20–30% stress difference are unsupported by the cited evidence and unrelated to the target outcomes.
A maximum strain of about 1% may remain largely elastic and therefore may be insufficient to assess yielding, dislocation accumulation, or strain hardening.
explanation: The response correctly identifies molecular dynamics as a possible method for studying mechanical behavior at atomistic resolution and includes stress–strain and dislocation measurements. However, it changes nearly every defining element of the target: polycrystal instead of an FCC single crystal, compression–tension asymmetry instead of tensile anisotropy, one nominal temperature and rate instead of systematic temperature/rate/orientation sweeps, and chemical ordering instead of Shockley-partial-mediated stacking faults. It misses the target findings of maximum yield stress along <-111>, thermal yield softening, yield-rate insensitivity, increasing dislocation density with rate, and absence of BCC transformation or twinning. The baseline is not an actual reference condition, and the proposed evidence is not transferable enough to support the central mechanism.
